newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Zaire rebels said offering gold mining concessions.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels said offering gold mining concessions.

text.p: Zairean rebels are already offering gold mining concessions in parts of the country they control to foreign companies, an investment analyst said on Monday.
Rebel leader Laurent Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL) seized most of the country's gold mines in eastern Zaire in January.

The rebels have also taken over Zairean leader Mobutu Sese Seko's personal gold mine and said earlier this month the gold mines they hold had resumed production and could help pay for their war effort.
Johannesburg-based investment analyst John Klemmow told Reuters that the rebels were now offering gold prospecting concessions.
"The rebels are already offering (gold) concessions and they only liberated these places a week or two ago -- you can see it is pretty open for business already," Klemmow said.
The rebels say their forces are 200 km (125 miles) from Zaire's second city Lubumbashi, capital of the southern copper mining province of Shaba.

Kabila's soldiers have taken over almost a fifth of the sprawling Central African country -- which mining analysts see as one of the richest mineral areas in the world -- since they took up arms in October.
The rebels have said Lubumbashi, centre of the country's copper and cobalt mining industry and base of the giant state mining company Gecamines, will be their next target.
Klemmow said he believed most of the country's mineral industry would be in rebel hands in the near future.
"Zaire's mineral industry is going to go (to the rebels)," he said.
